WWII veteran Maury Feren remember crawling over dead bodies from his time serving as a medic

As someone who had a grandfather (he passed away in 2012) that was a medic in WWII, I thank you for posting this. My grandfather rarely, mentioned anything about his time in WWII. Most of it was about the conditions (no food - he told me they had to catch and eat lizards and grasshoppers when I was little, rampant malaria, the mosquitoes and leeches), what the jungles were like, how their guides they initially had were great people (told them what lizards, bugs and plants were safe to eat), how the Japanese were brutal (all that I stated he said over my lifetime, never all at once). Nothing too in detail. Anything he offered up was short and general. He served 2 tours in the Philippines during the fight against Japan. When I asked him if he would like to talk about it more in detail, not long before he passed away, he said, "No, the stuff I witnessed and took part in no one should ever have to live through, even in hearing second hand. These memories will die with me, as they should have in that war. I have seen the best of humanity and the worst, but the best doesn't give you nightmares for a lifetime." I know he was trying to protect me from the horrors he went through, and I respect him for that. This bit of audio you posted and others I have heard like it, helps me to understand my grandfather better and what he kept locked away in his memories for a lifetime. Again, good post. Thank you.
